title: The Six Swans
text:
A king who had lost his way in a forest was rescued by a witch, on condition that he marry her daughter. He did, but he feared her, and he hid his six sons and one daughter, children of his first marriage, in a lonely castle. The new queen found out. She sewed six small white shirts with a spell in them, threw them over the boys, and they turned into swans and flew away.

The sister went in search of them. She learned that to break the spell she must not speak or laugh for six years, and must sew six shirts for them out of starwort flowers. If she said one word, all her work would be lost.

She sat in a tree and sewed. A king out hunting found her, fell in love with her and married her, though she never spoke. His mother hated the silent young queen. When she bore a child, the mother-in-law took it away, smeared the queen's mouth with blood and accused her of eating it. Two more times this happened. The queen could not defend herself without breaking her silence, and she was sentenced to be burned.

On the day of the fire, the six years ended. Six swans flew down. She threw the shirts over them and her brothers stood there as men, though the youngest kept a swan's wing where one sleeve was unfinished. Then at last she spoke, and told the king the truth.
lesson: Some of the most important things we do for family are slow, unseen and misunderstood. Keep faith with the work even when you cannot explain it.
people: A sister, her six brothers, the king, his mother
source: Brothers Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmarchen, No. 49 (Die sechs Schwane)
